newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index firms 0.51 pts on gains to VSZ.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index firms 0.51 pts on gains to VSZ.

text.p: Gains to shares of steel maker VSZ pushed the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday, as the SAX index firmed 0.51 points to 186.33.
VSZ closed up 10 crowns at 660, dominating activity on the BSE floor while bank VUB also gained 10 crowns to 1,710.
Brokers said activity overall was still quiet, with only VUB attracting significant investor interest.
"Despite Wednesday's insignificant volume, we see interest in VUB getting stronger," said Peter Lachkovic of Slovenska Sporitelna.
He said the demand for VUB might be boosted by investors speculating before the expected privatisation of the country's banking sector.
Oil and gas storage company Nafta was unchanged at 1,690 crowns and Lachkovic said the current Nafta's price appeared unattractive for shareholders to offer some bigger blocks of shares.
Overall volume eased to 266,926 shares, from 412,075 shares traded on Tuesday, while turnover decreased to 148.14 million crowns, from 188.84 million.
